top_story: The 9 September killing of 12 members of a single family in southern Lebanon, including six children, underscored how Israel’s continued strikes are hollowing out ceasefire diplomacy and deepening civilian trauma along the border. By 14 September, the conflict’s regional spillover hit energy infrastructure when a drone attack on a key Saudi pipeline threatened disruption of up to 4 percent of global oil supply and weeks of repairs, widening the economic stakes well beyond the battlefield. On 15 September, renewed fighting in Yemen had already displaced more than 100,000 people and pushed others across the Red Sea to Djibouti, showing how escalation is driving both market risk and mass civilian flight. The regional picture is of conflicts no longer contained within front lines, but increasingly linking local violence to cross-border displacement, economic vulnerability, and weakening deterrence.
